description: Create a new Status Page in OneUptime. Returns the created Status Page object with its ID. Use this to add new Status Pages to your project. Note: projectId is inferred from your API key — you do not need to provide it.

allowSubscribersToChooseEventTypes.description: Can subscribers choose which event type like Announcements, Incidents, Scheduled Events to subscribe to?

allowSubscribersToChooseResources.description: Can subscribers choose which resources to subscribe to?

allowedSubscriberEmailDomains.description: The domains an email subscriber's address may be at, one a line, such as acme.com. An address at a subdomain of one matches too. Sign-ups and additions at any other domain are refused, and an email subscriber at another domain is sent nothing. Empty: any domain.
allowedSubscriberEmailDomains.example: This is an example of very long text content that might be stored in this field. It can contain a lot of information, such as detailed descriptions, comments, or any other lengthy text data that needs to be stored in the database.

callSmsConfigId.description: ID of your Call/SMS Config Resource which is used to send SMS to subscribers.

coverImageAltText.description: Alternative text for the cover image, read by screen readers for accessibility. Leave blank if the cover image is purely decorative.

customCSS.description: Status Page Custom CSS. Served only from a verified custom domain.

customJavaScript.description: Status Page Custom JavaScript. This runs when the status page is loaded from a verified custom domain.

darkThemeLogoFileId.description: Status Page Dark Theme Logo File ID.

defaultBarColor.description: Default color of the bar on the overview page.

defaultLanguage.description: Default language that the status page is shown in when a visitor arrives for the first time.

description.description: Friendly description that will help you remember.
description.example: This is an example of longer text content that might be stored in this field.

embeddedOverallStatusToken.description: Security token required to access the embedded overall status badge. This token must be provided in the URL.

enableCustomSubscriberEmailNotificationF.description: Enable custom footer text in subscriber email notifications.

enableEmailSubscribers.description: Can email subscribers subscribe to this Status Page?

enableEmbeddedOverallStatus.description: Enable embedded overall status badge that can be displayed on external websites?

enableMasterPassword.description: Require visitors to enter a master password before viewing a private status page.

enableMcpServer.description: Can AI agents read this status page over the public OneUptime MCP server? This does not affect the status page website, its RSS feed, or its public JSON API.

enableMicrosoftTeamsSubscribers.description: Can Microsoft Teams subscribers subscribe to this Status Page?

enableSearchEngineIndexing.description: Should search engines like Google and Bing be allowed to index this status page? Turn this off to keep the page reachable by link but out of search results.

enableSlackSubscribers.description: Can Slack subscribers subscribe to this Status Page?

enableSmsSubscribers.description: Can SMS subscribers subscribe to this Status Page?

enableWebhookSubscribers.description: Can Webhook subscribers subscribe to this Status Page?

enabledLanguages.description: Languages offered in the footer language switcher. Leave empty to offer all supported languages.

footerHTML.description: Status Page Custom HTML Footer. Served only from a verified custom domain.

headerHTML.description: Status Page Custom HTML Header. Served only from a verified custom domain.

ipWhitelist.description: IP Whitelist for this Status Page. One IP per line. Only used if the status page is private.
ipWhitelist.example: This is an example of very long text content that might be stored in this field. It can contain a lot of information, such as detailed descriptions, comments, or any other lengthy text data that needs to be stored in the database.

isArchived.description: Archived status pages are hidden from the Status Pages list, are not served to visitors, and send nothing to their subscribers. Unarchiving puts them back online.

isReportEnabled.description: Whether this status page's email subscribers get reports. Turned on without a schedule, reports go out on the 1st of every month at 09:00 in the report timezone, each covering the calendar month before it.

labels.description: Relation to Labels Array where this object is categorized in.

limitSubscribersToPrivateUsers.description: Only people who can sign in to this status page can be its subscribers, each with the email address they sign in with: no other address, and no phone, Slack, Microsoft Teams or webhook. A subscriber whose address is not a private user of this page - one removed since, by SCIM or by hand - is sent nothing.

logoAltText.description: Alternative text for the logo image, read by screen readers for accessibility.

masterPassword.description: Password required to unlock a private status page. This value is stored as a secure hash.

name.description: Any friendly name of this object.

onlyShowScopedIncidents.description: When on, this status page shows and notifies its subscribers about only the incidents limited to it. Incidents that are not limited to any status page never reach it.

overallUptimePercentPrecision.description: Overall Precision of uptime percent for this status page.

overviewPageDescription.description: Overview Page description for your status page. This is a markdown field.

pageDescription.description: Description of your Status Page. This is used for SEO.
pageDescription.example: This is an example of longer text content that might be stored in this field.

pageTitle.description: Title of your Status Page. This is used for SEO.

privateUserSessionLengthInHours.description: How long, in hours, a private user stays signed in to this private status page after signing in, however active they are - with a password, SSO or OIDC. When the time is up they sign in again. Applies to readers signed in now too. A whole number from 1 to 8760; empty for no limit, where a reader stays signed in while they open the page at least once every 30 days.

projectId.description: ID of your OneUptime Project in which this object belongs.

reportDataInDays.description: How many days of data should be included in the report?

reportPeriodType.description: Should the report cover a rolling number of days, or the previous whole calendar period?

reportRecurringInterval.description: How often a report goes out. Left out when reports are turned on, it is every month.

reportStartDateTime.description: When the first report goes out. Every later one follows it by the recurring interval, at the same time of day. Left out when reports are turned on, it is 09:00 in the report timezone at the start of the next period of the interval: the next 1st of the month for a monthly schedule (the default), the next Monday for a weekly one, the next day for a daily one and the next 1 January for a yearly one. An hourly schedule starts at the next full hour.

reportTimezone.description: The timezone report periods and send times are resolved in. A monthly report in this timezone runs from the 1st at 00:00 to the last day at 23:59.

requireSsoForLogin.description: Should SSO be required to login to Private Status Page.

sendNextReportBy.description: When the next report goes out. The server works it out from the schedule.

sendSubscriberNotifications.description: Does this status page tell its subscribers anything? Off, it sends them nothing - no message about an incident, an episode, scheduled maintenance or an announcement, and no report - however the event was created. Its subscribers are kept, and the channel switches still decide how visitors can sign up.

showAnnouncementHistoryInDays.description: How many days of announcement history should be shown on the status page (in days)?

showEpisodeHistoryInDays.description: How many days of episode history to show on the status page.

showEpisodeLabelsOnStatusPage.description: Show Episode Labels on Status Page?

showEpisodesOnStatusPage.description: Show Incident Episodes on Status Page?

showIncidentHistoryInDays.description: How many days of incident history should be shown on the status page (in days)?

showIncidentLabelsOnStatusPage.description: Show Incident Labels on Status Page?

showOverallUptimePercentOnStatusPage.description: Show Overall Uptime Percent on Status Page?

showScheduledEventHistoryInDays.description: How many days of scheduled event history should be shown on the status page (in days)?

showScheduledEventLabelsOnStatusPage.description: Show Scheduled Event Labels on Status Page?

showScheduledMaintenanceEventsOnStatusPa.description: Show Scheduled Maintenance Events on Status Page?

showSubscriberPageOnStatusPage.description: Show Subscriber Page on Status Page?

showUptimeHistoryInDays.description: How many days of uptime history should be shown on the status page? Maximum is 90 days.

smtpConfigId.description: ID of your SMTP Config Resource which is used to send email to subscribers.

subscriberEmailNotificationFooterText.description: Text to send to subscribers in the footer of the email.
subscriberEmailNotificationFooterText.example: This is an example of very long text content that might be stored in this field. It can contain a lot of information, such as detailed descriptions, comments, or any other lengthy text data that needs to be stored in the database.

subscriberTimezones.description: Timezones of subscribers to this status page.

theme.description: How the status page looks to visitors: Light, Dark, or System (light or dark, as each visitor's device is set). A status page created without a theme starts with System.

name: create_status_page
title: Create Status Page
